title: Analysis By Deep Sequencing of Discontinued Neurotropic Yellow Fever Vaccine Strains.
ehr_evidence: Four examples of the FNV (FNV-IP, FNV-Yale, FNV-FC, FNV-NT), 17D-204 vaccine and wild-type parental strains Asibi and FVV were all subjected to next generation sequencing; viral RNAs were sequenced and analyzed by massively parallel, in silico methods from archived laboratory strains.
summary: An in silico deep-sequencing study of discontinued French neurotropic yellow fever vaccine strains compared with wild-type parental strains, showing that FNV is genetically unstable with variable reversion to wild-type associated with neurotropy.
key_findings: FNV vaccine strains were of lower normalized Shannon's entropy diversity than wild-type FVV (Kruskal-Wallis X² = 2773.51, df = 6, p < 0.001 for the ORF).
Pairwise Wilcoxon tests showed significant NSE differences between all strain pairs except Asibi/FNV-IP (p = 0.36), Asibi/FNV-NT (p = 0.11), FNV-FC/FNV-Yale (p = 0.53), and FNV-IP/FNV-NT (p = 0.5).
Loss of neurotropism in mice was associated with an abundance of wild-type RNA populations, and reversion to wild-type identity was variably observed across FNV strains.
Eight nucleotide positions were especially unstable, showing high diversity and high genetic distance from FVV in at least one FNV strain.
Highly neurotropic strains FNV-Yale and FNV-IP had fewer variants (n = 91 each) than low-neurotropism strains FNV-FC (131) and FNV-NT (165).
captured_features: nucleotide differences and amino acid substitutions vs wild-type FVV
study_design: in vitro/in silico comparative genomic study of archived viral strains (not a human cohort, case-control, or cross-sectional design)
data_source_type: biospecimen (archived viral vaccine strains subjected to next-generation sequencing)
population: Seven viral strains: four discontinued FNV vaccine strains (FNV-IP, FNV-Yale, FNV-FC, FNV-NT), the 17D-204 vaccine, and wild-type parental strains Asibi and FVV
exposure_domain: none (viral genetics/genomics; not an environmental exposome exposure)
limitations: Passage histories of the FNV strains were unavailable and their relationship to the original Dakar strain is unknown.
Very small sample size (n = 7 viral strains).
All strains were passaged once in Vero cells before sequencing, which may alter variant frequencies.
Neurotropic and viscerotropic determinants could not be cleanly parsed due to limited animal models.
data_availability_statement: Pre-reduction datasets from sequencing analyses are available from the authors upon request.
